headline_en: Can the Probashi Card bring positive change to the migration and remittance system?
summary_en: An opinion column on the Bangladesh government's planned Probashi Card (expatriate card), whose pilot is to start through state-owned Janata Bank in the month after August 2026. It lists the benefits the government has announced (reward points, credit scoring, airport and priority services, insurance, body transport) and argues the card should become a life-cycle digital service platform covering verified jobs, training, clearance, complaints and reintegration. It cites a RMMRU study that 40-45 percent of remittance comes through hundi.

facts.date: September 2026 (stated as 'next month' in a column published 31 Aug 2026)
facts.statement: The Bangladesh government is going to start a pilot of the Probashi Card (expatriate card) through state-owned Janata Bank in the month after August 2026.

facts.date: targets: December 2026 and June 2027 (stated as 'December of the current year' and 'June of next year')
facts.statement: The Probashi Card pilot aims to distribute 50,000 cards by December 2026 and 200,000 (2 lakh) cards by June of the following year.
The Probashi Card plan speaks of social status, financial incentives, and easier international payment and banking facilities for expatriate Bangladeshis.
The government has said it will introduce remittance reward points and credit scoring under the Probashi Card.

The announced Probashi Card benefits include priority in land registration and mutation (namjari), utility connections, licences, investment, national ID card, passport, consular and banking services.

The announced Probashi Card benefits also include airport lounge, special immigration booths, meet and greet, hospital services, transport of dead bodies, insurance and priority services; the columnist says clear procedures are still needed on whether the special booths are really faster, where the hospital benefit can be used and how fast insurance claims are settled.
According to a study by the Refugee and Migratory Movements Research Unit (RMMRU), 40-45 percent of remittance to Bangladesh comes through hundi (informal transfer).
facts.source_in_article: RMMRU study, cited by the columnist

facts.statement: The columnist notes that many expatriates send money home for years but banks cannot assess their financial capacity because they have no conventional salary account or loan history; he proposes that remittance amount and regularity be made part of a financial profile banks can use for loan risk assessment.

The columnist recommends a verified overseas job database (demand by country and occupation, skills, salary, employer, recruitment cost, contract length) with no job posted without verification by a Bangladesh mission or authorised authority, and a digital profile holding BMET registration, training and skill certificates, medical report, insurance, job contract, salary, migration cost and clearance so a worker can check before going to the airport that the terms in government records match the real contract. These are proposals, not existing services.

The columnist proposes a central digital system for complaints, insurance claims and emergency help for workers abroad, with complaints trackable and automatically forwarded to the Bangladesh mission, BMET or the Wage Earners' Welfare Board, and a national database of returnees' skills with formal recognition through 'recognition of prior learning'. These are proposals, not existing services.

The column states that many Bangladeshis who go to the Middle East as labourers and domestic workers are exploited and abused, and that Bangladesh still sends a very large number of unskilled and semi-skilled workers abroad while demand for skilled and specialised workers is rising fast.

headline_en: One Bangladeshi worker killed, another missing in explosion at gas complex in Russia
summary_en: A gas explosion at the Amur Gas Chemical Complex in Russia's Amur region killed at least 15 people, including one Bangladeshi worker; another Bangladeshi is missing and seven were injured. The Bangladesh Embassy in Moscow named the victims, said the injured are being moved to a specialised hospital in Moscow, and opened a 24-hour hotline.

facts.statement: A gas explosion at the Amur Gas Chemical Complex in Russia's Amur region killed one Bangladeshi worker, left one Bangladeshi missing and injured seven Bangladeshis; at least 15 people died in total.

facts.date: body recovered Thursday morning, about 27 Aug 2026
facts.statement: The Bangladeshi worker killed in the Amur Gas Chemical Complex explosion in Russia was Zakir Hossain of Bhairab, Kishoreganj; his body was recovered on Thursday morning.

The Bangladeshi worker missing after the Amur Gas Chemical Complex explosion in Russia is Md. Alal Hossain Raju of Gangni, Meherpur. Several bodies were burnt beyond identification and he may be among them.

The Amur Gas Chemical Complex in Russia, where Bangladeshi workers were employed, is operated under China's Sinopec Engineering Group, according to the Bangladesh Embassy in Moscow. It is one of the world's largest polyethylene and polypropylene producers, with capacity of up to 2.7 million tonnes a year.

The seven injured Bangladeshi workers from the Amur explosion are being taken from Amur to a specialised hospital in Moscow for better treatment; six of them are in intensive care (ICU). The Bangladesh Embassy in Moscow said it will oversee their treatment once they are in Moscow.

The Bangladesh Embassy in Moscow opened a 24-hour hotline for information on and help for Bangladeshis affected by the Amur explosion: +79162323015 (Counsellor and Head of Chancery) and +79891139169 (First Secretary, Labour Welfare Wing).

headline_en: Prime Minister urges Anwar Ibrahim to open Malaysia's labour market quickly
summary_en: At a joint press conference in Putrajaya on Monday 22 June 2026, Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman said he had asked Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim to consider hiring more Bangladeshi workers and opening the labour market quickly, and had raised regularisation of irregular workers and repatriation of detained Bangladeshis. The two sides agreed recruitment must be transparent, fair and affordable. The rest of the article covers trade, investment, MoUs, Rohingya and ASEAN matters.

facts.statement: On Monday 22 June 2026, at a joint press conference at the Malaysian Prime Minister's Office in Putrajaya, Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman said he had asked Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim to consider recruiting more Bangladeshi workers and opening the labour market quickly. The article reports a request, not a reopening.
Tarique Rahman said he also raised with Anwar Ibrahim the regularisation of irregular (undocumented) Bangladeshi workers in Malaysia and the possible repatriation of detained Bangladeshis.
Tarique Rahman said Bangladesh and Malaysia agreed that the worker recruitment process must be transparent, fair and affordable so that the role of middlemen shrinks and workers' costs fall.

After the Bangladesh-Malaysia bilateral meeting on 22 June 2026, a memorandum of understanding on culture was signed and documents on counter-terrorism research and capacity building and on investment were exchanged; manpower, education and skills development were among the sectors discussed. No labour agreement was reported signed.

The Bangladesh delegation to the 22 June 2026 Malaysia meeting included Foreign Minister Khalilur Rahman, Overseas Employment Minister Ariful Haque, and Mahdi Amin, adviser on education and overseas employment.

headline_en: Dubai company to hire 6,000 taxi drivers from Bangladesh; state minister urges cutting cost to BDT 1 lakh
summary_en: Dubai Taxi Company told Bangladesh's expatriates' welfare ministry on 17 May 2026 that it wants to hire 6,000 skilled drivers from Bangladesh in 2026, including 1,500 in the current round, with interviews starting 18 May 2026 at the Bangladesh-Korea Technical Training Centre. State Minister Md. Nurul Haque asked that the migration cost for a driver be kept within BDT 1 lakh, and the minister asked the company to pay salary during training in Dubai. Al Anas Overseas was named as the only approved recruiting agency for the company.

facts.statement: Dubai Taxi Company will newly recruit 6,000 skilled drivers from Bangladesh during 2026; its delegation said it is interested in hiring 6,000 drivers this year including a further 1,500 in the current round. This was stated at a courtesy meeting with Minister Ariful Haque Chowdhury at the Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment in Dhaka on Sunday 17 May 2026.
facts.source_in_article: Dubai Taxi Company delegation, at the Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment

facts.statement: Interviews to screen and select qualified Bangladeshi drivers for Dubai Taxi Company start on Monday 18 May 2026 at the Bangladesh-Korea Technical Training Centre.

Dubai Taxi Company representatives said about 15,000 workers from 27 countries currently work for the company as taxi and limousine drivers, of whom about 8,000 are Bangladeshi; they said Bangladeshi workers are given priority in hiring because they are very hardworking.
Dubai Taxi Company representatives said Bangladeshi women are also working successfully as drivers at Dubai airport.

State Minister for Expatriates' Welfare Md. Nurul Haque said it currently costs a driver 'a lot of money' to go from Bangladesh to Dubai (no figure given) and specially requested that this migration cost be reduced and kept within BDT 1 lakh (100,000 taka). This was a request, not a set fee.

Minister Ariful Haque Chowdhury called on Dubai Taxi Company to arrange salary and allowances for workers during the training period after they arrive in Dubai. The article does not say the company agreed.

'Al Anas Overseas' is described as the only approved recruiting agency for sending workers to Dubai Taxi Company in the United Arab Emirates; its representatives said they are also interested in taking cleaners, technicians and mechanics from Bangladesh besides drivers.
Minister Ariful Haque Chowdhury also asked Dubai Taxi Company to recruit doctors, nurses and other professionals from Bangladesh.

headline_en: Cases filed against 9 brokers at two police stations in Sunamganj
summary_en: After 12 young men from Sunamganj died on a rubber boat that left Libya for Greece on 21 March 2026, two cases under the human trafficking law were filed on 30 March 2026 against nine brokers at Jagannathpur and Derai police stations. The boat ran out of fuel, lost its way and drifted for six days; many died of dehydration and starvation and the bodies were put into the sea. The victims had paid BDT 10-20 lakh each.

facts.statement: Two cases under the Prevention and Suppression of Human Trafficking Act were filed against nine brokers in Sunamganj over the deaths of 12 people on a Libya-Greece sea crossing: five accused at Jagannathpur police station and four at Derai police station.
facts.source_in_article: Sunamganj Additional Superintendent of Police Sujan Sarkar

facts.statement: Sunamganj Additional Superintendent of Police Sujan Sarkar said police are not disclosing the names of the accused brokers for now and that police operations to catch them are continuing.
facts.source_in_article: Additional Superintendent of Police Sujan Sarkar

facts.statement: The plaintiff in the Derai police station case is Salikur Rahman, father of Sohanur Rahman of Basuri village, Jagdal union, Derai upazila, who died in the Mediterranean; the plaintiff in the Jagannathpur case is Habibur Rahman of Pailgaon village, Pailgaon union, whose son Aminur Rahman died the same way.
On 21 March 2026 a small rubber boat left Libya for Greece with 48 people aboard. Its fuel ran out first, then it lost its way and was at sea for six days.
facts.source_in_article: a surviving young man and families of the dead, as told to Prothom Alo

facts.statement: Many people on the Libya-Greece rubber boat died of dehydration and starvation during six days at sea, including 12 from Sunamganj, all young men. The bodies were kept on the boat for two days and then put into the sea by their companions.
facts.source_in_article: a surviving young man and families of the dead

facts.statement: On 27 March 2026 the Greek coast guard rescued 22 people alive from the boat drifting off the Greek coast. News reached the relatives of the dead the next day, Saturday afternoon (28 March 2026).
facts.source_in_article: a surviving young man and families of the dead

facts.statement: Of the 12 Sunamganj men who died on the Libya-Greece crossing, 6 were from Derai upazila, 5 from Jagannathpur upazila and 1 from Dowarabazar upazila.
The Sunamganj men who died trying to reach Greece via Libya had paid BDT 10-20 lakh each to brokers; many sold cattle and land to raise the money.
A broker ring has grown up in Sunamganj district to take people to Europe by irregular routes, with associates in Libya, according to Prothom Alo's inquiry.

Sunamganj Deputy Commissioner Mohammad Ilias Mia said the UNOs (upazila executive officers) of Jagannathpur and Derai have made lists of brokers and given them to police, and inquiries are under way in all upazilas.

headline_en: Updates on expanding overseas labour markets must be presented every week: expatriates' welfare minister
summary_en: At the first meeting of a committee on increasing overseas employment and expatriate welfare on Wednesday 4 March 2026, Minister Ariful Haque Chowdhury ordered weekly update reports on expanding overseas labour markets and called Japan a promising market. The meeting was told Japan takes foreign workers in four main visa categories and, per a Japan Times report, will hire over 1.2 million foreign workers by 2029 in two of them. It was proposed to introduce Japanese language courses in all TTCs in phases.

facts.statement: Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment Minister Ariful Haque Chowdhury ordered that an updated report on expansion of overseas labour markets be presented every week from now on, at the first meeting of the committee formed on increasing overseas employment and expatriate welfare, held at the ministry in Dhaka on Wednesday 4 March 2026.

Minister Ariful Haque Chowdhury said Japan is a promising labour market for Bangladesh because of its demand for foreign workers, safe work environment, 100 percent labour rights and assurance of high wages, and that an action plan to increase employment in Japan is being prepared.
facts.source_in_article: Minister Ariful Haque Chowdhury, via ministry press release

facts.statement: According to information presented at the Bangladesh ministry meeting, Japan takes foreign workers mainly in four visa categories: Employment for Skill Development (ESD), Specified Skilled Worker (SSW), Engineers/Specialist in Humanities/International Services, and Student.
facts.source_in_article: information presented at the ministry committee meeting

facts.statement: According to a Japan Times report cited at the meeting, Japan will recruit more than 1.2 million (12 lakh) foreign workers by 2029 in the ESD and SSW categories alone.
facts.source_in_article: Japan Times report, cited at the ministry meeting

facts.statement: The meeting was told that, according to Bangladesh's latest census, about 2.5 crore working-age people are surplus even after meeting domestic labour-market demand.
facts.source_in_article: information presented at the ministry committee meeting

facts.statement: The meeting was told that with proper preparation and confirmed demand from Japanese companies, it may be possible to send more than one lakh new workers from Bangladesh to Japan by 2030.
facts.source_in_article: information presented at the ministry committee meeting

facts.statement: A proposal was raised at the meeting to introduce Japanese language courses in all Technical Training Centres (TTCs) in phases; recruiting the needed number of local Japanese-language trainers and connecting Japanese trainers through a 'virtual teaching' platform were also discussed. headline_en: War has spread: what will happen to Bangladesh's labour market in the Middle East
summary_en: After joint US-Israeli strikes on Iran, war spread across the Middle East in early March 2026; airspace closures cancelled flights, stranded many Bangladeshi workers and virtually halted new deployment to the six GCC countries. Two Bangladeshi workers were reported killed and seven injured. Qatar extended all expired or expiring visas by one month from 28 February 2026, automatically and free. The article gives numbers of Bangladeshi workers in each GCC country and the GCC share of remittance.

facts.statement: After the joint US-Israeli attack on Iran and the spread of war in the Middle East, two Bangladeshi workers in the Gulf region had been reported killed and seven more injured as of 4 March 2026.

Because air links were shut, sending new workers from Bangladesh to the six Gulf (GCC) countries, Saudi Arabia, United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Kuwait, Bahrain and Oman, had virtually come to a standstill as of 4 March 2026.
According to government statistics, about 45 lakh (4.5 million) Bangladeshis currently work in the six GCC countries.

According to Expatriates' Welfare Ministry statistics, Bangladeshi workers number about 20 lakh in Saudi Arabia, 10 lakh in the United Arab Emirates, 7 lakh in Oman, 4 lakh 50 thousand in Qatar, 1 lakh 50 thousand in Bahrain and 1 lakh 40 thousand in Kuwait.

According to Bangladesh Bank, total remittance in the first quarter (July-September) of fiscal year 2025-26 was about 759 crore and about 344 crore of it came from the six GCC countries, 45.40 percent of the total (the article prints the unit as taka). Elsewhere the article gives the same 45.40 percent as the GCC share for 'fiscal year 2025-26'.

According to Bangladesh missions in Saudi Arabia, Qatar and Bahrain, Middle Eastern countries closed their airspace after the conflict, scheduled flights were cancelled and many workers were stranded. Workers who had come home to Bangladesh on leave or for emergencies were also stuck and their return was uncertain.
facts.source_in_article: Bangladesh missions in Saudi Arabia, Qatar and Bahrain

facts.statement: In some Middle Eastern countries the visas of Bangladeshi workers, especially entry visas, were close to expiring during the flight shutdown, causing growing anxiety among them.

Several Bangladesh foreign ministry officials said that although new workers' travel to the Middle East was almost uncertain for now, visa and flight problems would be resolved; Qatar had already extended entry visas by one month and other countries had taken visa extension under consideration.
facts.source_in_article: several Ministry of Foreign Affairs officials

facts.statement: A government official, speaking anonymously, said workers whose flights were cancelled and who had bought Biman Bangladesh tickets would have their tickets rescheduled, and other airlines had been requested to reschedule Bangladeshi workers' tickets as well.

Qatar's Ministry of Interior decided to extend by one month the validity of all types of visas that had expired or were about to expire; the decision took effect from 28 February 2026 for the following month and the period may be extended further depending on the situation.
facts.source_in_article: Qatar Ministry of Interior; Bangladesh Embassy in Qatar and Doha News

facts.statement: Qatar's Ministry of Interior said the visa extension is done automatically through the electronic system: no fee has to be paid, and there is no need to appear at any office or submit any application.
For visas in Qatar that expired before 28 February 2026, the one-month extension applies only after the prescribed fine has been paid.

According to diplomatic sources, at a briefing the Qatar government held for foreign diplomats on Monday, most countries asked for visa validity to be extended, and Qatar took the request into account in deciding to extend entry visas by one month.
People concerned said that if the Middle East conflict is prolonged, new overseas employment may fall and remittance flow may slow, affecting Bangladesh's overall economy.

headline_en: 90 percent of workers who went abroad last year went to 5 countries: RMMRU
summary_en: RMMRU's report 'Trends of Labour Migration from Bangladesh 2025: Achievements and Challenges', released on 7 January 2026 at the National Press Club in Dhaka, says 1,130,757 workers went abroad in 2025, 67 percent of them to Saudi Arabia and 90 percent to five countries. It covers falling female migration, record remittance, the rise of Russia as a market with a ring sending workers to the Russia-Ukraine war, sea arrivals in Italy, the Malaysia syndicate and the growth in recruiting agency licences.

facts.statement: According to government data cited by RMMRU, Bangladeshi workers went to 141 countries in 2025, but 90 percent went to just 5 countries; one worker each went to 13 countries and 2 to 10 workers each went to 34 countries.
facts.source_in_article: RMMRU report 'Trends of Labour Migration from Bangladesh 2025', using government data

facts.statement: RMMRU's report says 1,130,757 (11 lakh 30 thousand 757) workers went abroad from Bangladesh in 2025, about 12 percent more than the previous year.
67 percent of all Bangladeshi migrant workers in 2025 went to Saudi Arabia, a total of 754,369 people; next were Qatar with 10 percent, Singapore 6 percent, Kuwait 4 percent and Maldives 4 percent.
RMMRU says there is a count of how many workers have gone abroad since 1976 but no count of returnees, so the total number of workers currently abroad is not known.

62,317 Bangladeshi women workers went abroad in 2025, 1.9 percent more than the previous year. More than one lakh women went each year from 2016 to 2019; the number fell for two years because of Covid, passed one lakh again in 2022 and has been falling since.

RMMRU's report says female migration from Bangladesh in 2025 also took place to Qatar, Brunei, United Arab Emirates, South Korea, Kuwait, Hong Kong and Japan, though numbers to Hong Kong and Japan were very small; it says uncertainty about decent workplaces and violence against women inside households keep discouraging female migration.

RMMRU says remittance has grown about 10 percent each year and USD 3,282 crore came in 2025, the highest in 25 years; among the top 10 countries, Saudi Arabia accounted for the most at 15.52 percent and the United Arab Emirates 12.58 percent.
RMMRU says the migration sector's allocation in the last fiscal year's national budget was 0.08 percent and that the current government has cut it further.
RMMRU noted that for the first time Bangladeshi migrants are about to get the chance to vote while staying abroad, calling it a historic step.

RMMRU acting executive director Tasneem Siddiqui said 252 new recruiting agency licences were issued and another 300 are in process. The report says Bangladesh earlier had 850 to 900 agencies, the previous government raised this to 2,300, and 252 more were approved in 2025.
facts.source_in_article: Tasneem Siddiqui, RMMRU acting executive director; RMMRU report

facts.statement: RMMRU's report says the number of recruiting agencies is 192 in India, 464 in Pakistan, 416 in Nepal and 248 in Sri Lanka, which is easy to monitor.
RMMRU's report calls Russia an important new labour market for Bangladesh: 4,663 Bangladeshis went there in 2025 against 993 the year before.

RMMRU's report says a ring has begun recruiting migrants with the lure of good pay and Russian citizenship, and part of this ring, together with a dishonest ring in Russia, is sending Bangladeshi workers to the Russia-Ukraine war.

From 1 January to 3 October 2025, 15,076 Bangladeshi migrants reached Italy's coast by sea, the highest among all nationalities arriving in Italy in that year and nearly double the previous year's figure.

RMMRU's report says the process of opening the Malaysian labour market has recently started, and that trying to reopen it through the ringleaders of the old syndicate without punishing them is unacceptable.
RMMRU's report says several closed labour markets including Oman and Bahrain could not be reopened in 2025, and the United Arab Emirates market has still not opened in any real way.
RMMRU's report says that during the current (interim) government's time a total of 7 agreements were signed with Italy, South Korea, Japan and Saudi Arabia to expand labour markets.

RMMRU demanded that the number of licensed recruiting agencies be reduced systematically, that licences be confiscated where family members hold more than one and from those who resort to fraud in recruitment, and that 1 percent of the national budget or 5 percent of annual remittance be allocated to the migration sector. It also said Bangladesh should be sending workers regularly to at least 8-10 markets.
Tasneem Siddiqui said new labour markets are not being created because skills are not being improved, and that if skilled workers are produced markets will not have to be sought.

headline_en: Boat carrying 26 Bangladeshis sinks off Libya coast, 4 dead
summary_en: The Libyan Red Crescent said two boats carrying migrants and asylum seekers sank near the coastal city of Al-Khums on the night of Thursday 13 November 2025; the first carried 26 people from Bangladesh, four of whom died. The article also lists other recent migrant boat disasters off Libya and a UN meeting call to close Libyan detention centres where migrants are tortured.

facts.statement: Two boats carrying migrants and asylum seekers sank near the Libyan coastal city of Al-Khums; the first boat carried 26 people from Bangladesh, of whom four died, according to a Libyan Red Crescent Society statement issued on Saturday 15 November 2025.
The second boat that sank near Al-Khums, Libya carried 69 people, including two Egyptians and many Sudanese and eight children; their fate was not clear.

Al-Khums, where the boat with 26 Bangladeshis sank, is a coastal city about 118 km east of the Libyan capital Tripoli. Since the fall of Muammar Gaddafi in 2011, Libya has become the main transit route for Europe-bound migrants and asylum seekers.

The coast guard and the Al-Khums Port Security Agency took part in the rescue after the Al-Khums sinking, and the bodies were handed to the relevant authorities on the order of the city's public prosecutor.
The International Organization for Migration (IOM) said at least 42 migrants went missing and are presumed dead after a rubber boat sank near the Al Buri oilfield off Libya's north-north-west coast.

In mid-October 2025 the bodies of 61 migrants were recovered on the coast west of Tripoli; in September 2025 IOM said at least 50 people died after a fire on a boat carrying 75 Sudanese refugees off Libya.

At a UN meeting in Geneva, several countries including the United Kingdom, Spain, Norway and Sierra Leone called on Libya to close detention centres where, according to human rights organisations, migrants and refugees are tortured, beaten and sometimes killed.

summary_en: On Thursday 21 August 2025 CID arrested Sakhawat Hossain (42), accused in human trafficking cases, at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport when he arrived among 175 Bangladeshis sent home from Libya on embassy out-passes by charter flight. CID says he ran a mafia syndicate in Libya and admitted sending 400 to 500 Bangladeshis to Italy on four boats. He named other traffickers including a Biman Bangladesh Airlines traffic helper.

headline_en: 188 expatriates jailed for joining processions have returned home
summary_en: Bangladeshi expatriates who protested in the United Arab Emirates on 19 July 2024 in solidarity with the student uprising were arrested and jailed because unpermitted demonstrations are banned there; after Chief Adviser Muhammad Yunus requested clemency, 188 have been freed and returned home. Returnees say about 23 are still in jail and that they left behind unpaid wages, businesses and savings. The government marked 2 August 2025 as 'Remittance Fighters Day' and has given returnees cash support through the ministry and the Wage Earners' Welfare Board.

facts.statement: Any kind of procession or protest gathering without permission is completely banned in the United Arab Emirates; the country's law gives no scope for holding a protest programme without permission.

Bangladeshi expatriates in the United Arab Emirates demonstrated on 19 July 2024 in solidarity with the student movement in Bangladesh; as a result 57 people were detained in one case and police detained 56 in another case.
Of the first 57 Bangladeshis detained over the UAE protest, a court sentenced three to life imprisonment, 53 to 10 years and one to 11 years in prison.

facts.date: 28 August 2024; returns from first week of September 2024
facts.statement: On 28 August 2024 Chief Adviser Professor Muhammad Yunus spoke by telephone with UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan and requested that the Bangladeshis' sentences be waived; the UAE government responded, the prisoners were released in stages under a government pardon and began returning home from the first week of September 2024.

So far 188 Bangladeshi workers have been released from jail and returned home (the article says from the United Arab Emirates in one place and from the Middle East in another, citing the Expatriates' Welfare Ministry).
facts.source_in_article: Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment

facts.statement: Several expatriates who returned from the United Arab Emirates told Prothom Alo that about 23 people who took part in the protest are still in jail there.
There are more than 10 lakh (one million) Bangladeshis in the United Arab Emirates.

Six returnees from the UAE told Prothom Alo they came home leaving behind unpaid wages, businesses and savings; they said the government promised rehabilitation but they had to agitate after returning to claim their rights, though they received financial support in two rounds.

On 28 December 2024, at an event, Expatriates' Welfare Adviser Professor Asif Nazrul handed BDT 50,000 in cash each to 186 returned expatriate workers; after that the Wage Earners' Welfare Board also gave them financial support (amount not stated).

On the ministry's instruction the Wage Earners' Welfare Board began work in 2024 to help workers returned after the UAE protests: it made lists of returnees in different districts and collected their rehabilitation needs. Most workers wanted to go abroad again; those staying asked for business support; some asked for help repaying earlier debts.
facts.source_in_article: reporter, citing the Wage Earners' Welfare Board's work

facts.statement: The interim government observed 'Remittance Fighters Day' on Saturday 2 August 2025 with a special event at the International Mother Language Institute, Segunbagicha, Dhaka, organised by the Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment. Adviser Asif Nazrul said the government arranged special honours for those who lost jobs and returned from the Middle East for expressing solidarity with the uprising.

Bangladeshi expatriates held solidarity protests in many countries during the July-August 2024 uprising, including the UK, USA, Canada, Australia, most European countries, and Bangladeshis in South Korea, Japan, Maldives, Saudi Arabia, Qatar and Malaysia voiced support.

headline_en: Malaysia has introduced multiple-entry visa facility for Bangladeshi workers: Asif Nazrul
summary_en: Adviser Asif Nazrul said on 15 July 2025 that Malaysia has introduced multiple-entry visas for Bangladeshi workers through a circular issued on 10 July 2025 on behalf of the Director General of Malaysian Immigration. Workers already holding a single-entry visa and a PLKS need not apply afresh; the multiple-entry visa is issued automatically at PLKS renewal, and those with a valid PLKS can travel in and out meanwhile.

facts.statement: On 10 July 2025 the Malaysian government issued a circular, signed on behalf of the Director General of Malaysian Immigration, introducing the multiple-entry visa facility for Bangladeshi workers in Malaysia.
facts.source_in_article: Adviser Asif Nazrul, via Chief Adviser's press wing message

facts.statement: Bangladeshi workers who were issued a single-entry visa and a Temporary Employment Visit Pass (PLKS) before the circular do not need to apply for a new multiple-entry visa; the multiple-entry visa will be issued automatically when the PLKS is renewed.

Bangladeshi workers in Malaysia who had a single-entry visa and whose PLKS is valid can now travel between Malaysia and Bangladesh without a new multiple-entry visa; instructions on this have been given by circular to all international airports and land ports of Malaysia.
Asif Nazrul said Malaysia takes workers from 15 countries and only Bangladeshi workers were being given single-entry visas instead of multiple-entry visas, which caused them much hardship.

During a visit to Malaysia in May 2025, a delegation led by Adviser Asif Nazrul and the Chief Adviser's special envoy on international affairs Lutfey Siddiqi met Malaysia's home minister, who gave assurance of a quick solution to the visa problem; the ministry and the Bangladesh embassy in Malaysia then followed up continuously.

headline_en: Japan to take 1 lakh workers from Bangladesh
summary_en: At the 'Bangladesh Seminar on Human Resources' in Tokyo on Thursday 29 May 2025, Japanese authorities and business people said they would recruit at least one lakh workers from Bangladesh over the next five years. Chief Adviser Muhammad Yunus witnessed two memoranda of understanding between BMET and Japanese bodies. Speakers noted a shortage of Japanese language teachers in Bangladesh.

facts.statement: Japanese authorities and business people said they would recruit at least one lakh (100,000) workers from Bangladesh over the next five years to deal with Japan's growing labour shortage; NBCC chairman Mikio Kesagayama said 'in the next five years we are ready to welcome one lakh Bangladeshi workers'.

facts.statement: At the Tokyo seminar Chief Adviser Muhammad Yunus witnessed two memoranda of understanding: one between Bangladesh's Bureau of Manpower, Employment and Training (BMET) and Kaicom Dream Street (KDS), a Japan-Bangladesh joint venture; the other between BMET, Japan's National Business Support Combined Cooperatives (a federation of more than 65 companies in Japan) and JBBRA (Japan Bangla Bridge Recruiting Agency).
Chief Adviser Muhammad Yunus said the interim government will do everything necessary to create employment opportunities for Bangladeshis in Japan.

Watami Group president Miki Watanabe said a school the group established in Bangladesh trains 1,500 students a year and they plan to raise this to 3,000; he said people with technical education in Bangladesh will be able to enter Japan's job market.
Hiroaki Yagi, chairman of the Japan International Trainee and Skilled Worker Cooperation Organization (JITCO), said Bangladesh still has a shortage of (Japanese) language teachers.
Bangladesh's ambassador to Japan Md. Daud Ali said Japan's labour shortage may reach 1 crore 10 lakh (11 million) by 2040, an opportunity for Bangladesh to send more skilled workers.

Niki Hirobumi, state minister at Japan's Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare (MHLW), said Japan's population is declining and so it will need the help of Bangladeshi workers. Mitsuru Matsushita, representative director of a supervising organisation of a work-environment improvement cooperative in Shizuoka, said many Japanese companies are showing interest in Bangladeshis.

headline_en: Awami League loyalists being dropped, but attempt to re-form the 'Malaysia syndicate'
summary_en: Recruiting agency owners say the old syndicate controlling worker recruitment to Malaysia, led by Ruhul Amin (Swapan) and Aminul Islam (Amin Noor), is trying to re-form with new agencies as the interim government prepares talks to reopen the market, closed since June 2024. The ACC is investigating four former MPs in the syndicate; its summary says workers paid on average BDT 544,000 against a government maximum of BDT 78,990. The article explains how agency selection under the MoU and the FWCMS software works, and reports demands to amend the MoU.

facts.date: closed since June 2024; as of 18 April 2025
facts.statement: Malaysia's labour market has been closed to Bangladeshi workers since June 2024; worker recruitment to Malaysia has been halted more than once because of irregularities by the syndicate. As of April 2025 the interim government had taken the initiative to begin talks to reopen it and a government delegation might go to Malaysia soon.

The last date for approved Bangladeshi workers to travel to Malaysia was 31 May 2024. 17,000 workers who had completed all procedures could not go by then; BAIRA members say about 50,000 workers who had deposited money and were in process were harmed.
Many Bangladeshi workers who did reach Malaysia found no work; some are living in inhuman conditions and some returned empty-handed.
According to an Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC/Dudok) summary, the government-set maximum cost for sending a worker from Bangladesh to Malaysia is BDT 78,990.

facts.date: about 2022-2024 (the one and a half years the market was open)
facts.statement: According to the ACC summary, a Bangladeshi worker had to pay on average BDT 544,000 to go to Malaysia, and about 4.5 lakh workers were sent in one and a half years, generating business of BDT 24,000 crore; a subheading says workers lost seven times the money because of the syndicate.

A memorandum submitted by BAIRA members to the Expatriates' Welfare Ministry on 5 February 2025 says the syndicate built by Ruhul Amin and Aminul Islam extorted BDT 107,000 per person for sending workers to Malaysia last time.

Workers are recruited to Malaysia under a memorandum of understanding which says the Malaysian government selects the Bangladeshi recruiting agencies, through an online automatic process, from a list sent by the Bangladesh government. Under this syndicate system only certain agencies may send workers; many other agencies pay syndicate agencies to send workers in their name. The article says no other destination country has this system.

People concerned say Bangladesh sent Malaysia a list of 1,520 recruiting agencies; 25 were approved at first and this was raised in three rounds to 100, with large sums changing hands for each name added.

The automatic selection is done through the Foreign Workers Centralized Management System (FWCMS) via software named Migrams (মাইগ্রাম), owned by Bestinet, the company of Aminul Islam. The company is supposed to get 100 Malaysian ringgit or BDT 2,500 per worker, but is alleged to have done illegal business by controlling the whole process in the name of agency selection.

The Anti-Corruption Commission has begun investigating four former MPs who were in the Malaysia syndicate: former finance minister A H M Mustafa Kamal, former Feni MPs Nizam Uddin Hazari and Lt Gen (retd) Masud Uddin Chowdhury, and former Dhaka MP Benzir Ahmed. No action had yet been taken against the alleged ringleaders Ruhul Amin (Swapan) and Aminul Islam (Amin Noor) as of April 2025.

BAIRA members allege that last time the syndicate ringleaders took BDT 5 crore each in advance as security deposit from syndicate member agencies, and that this time they will take 50 lakh Malaysian ringgit (BDT 12.5 crore) each, to be adjusted once worker sending starts. Agency owners say at least two lists of agencies to be in the new syndicate have been found.
Ruhul Amin told Prothom Alo the allegation of forming a syndicate is not true and is a rumour created by one group; Aminul Islam could not be reached.

According to Expatriates' Welfare Ministry sources, a meeting of the Bangladesh-Malaysia joint technical committee was due in Dhaka on 22 May 2025, and a high-level ministry delegation might go to Malaysia for talks, with no date fixed.

The existing Bangladesh-Malaysia memorandum of understanding is valid until August 2026; if worker sending starts within that period, agency selection remains in Malaysia's hands, though the clause could be amended by agreement at renewal.

Joint Secretary (employment wing) A Z M Nurul Haque of the Expatriates' Welfare Ministry said there is no scope for forming a syndicate over the Malaysian market, the ministry wants all agencies to be able to take part, and amendment of some matters in the MoU will be discussed in the meeting with Malaysia.

facts.statement: Andy Hall, a UK national working on migration and human rights in Asia, said in a statement on his website on 7 April 2025 that moves are again under way in Bangladesh to form a syndicate over the Malaysian labour market and that the clauses handing control to the syndicate must be amended.

RMMRU founding chair Tasneem Siddiqui said the syndicate has repeatedly traded freely on the country's poor, must not be allowed to re-form on the pretext of the MoU, that Malaysia should take workers from Bangladesh under the same rules as from other countries, and that the government could sign a new bilateral agreement. Former BAIRA joint secretary general Fakhrul Islam said paying the syndicate to send workers will no longer be accepted and threatened a strong movement.

headline_en: Hometown app built by a Bangladeshi engineer is the new reliance of expatriates in Singapore
summary_en: A feature on the 'Hometown' app made by Go Zayan, the startup of Bangladeshi engineer Ridwan Hafiz, which lets Bangladeshi workers in Singapore buy air tickets (since December 2022) and send remittances home (since November 2023) in Bangla from their phones. Two workers describe booking a next-morning flight at night and sending about BDT 5 lakh home within 15 minutes. The app charges a flat 3 Singapore dollars per transfer and is working to expand to Malaysia and Saudi Arabia.

facts.statement: The 'Hometown' app, made by Go Zayan (the venture of Bangladeshi engineer-entrepreneur Ridwan Hafiz), was launched in December 2022 only for Bangladeshi expatriates in Singapore, at first for buying air tickets; it has a Bangla interface alongside English and a hotline where users can speak in their own language.

To use the Hometown app in Singapore, a user downloads it and verifies an account with their ID; passport, photo and similar details are taken when the account is opened, so no further information is needed to buy a ticket. The account is linked to the user's Singapore bank account; in line with Singapore law the app gives a QR code which the user saves on the phone and uploads in their bank's app, and the ticket price is paid automatically and the ticket issued.

Mahbub Alam, a user in Singapore, said the whole ticket purchase on the Hometown app takes at most three minutes without going anywhere, and that on checking he found he was given the ticket at a fair price with no extra charge.

Hometown added a remittance (money transfer to Bangladesh) service to its app in November 2023, after meeting financial rules in Singapore and Bangladesh including account-holder KYC, a digital link from Singapore to a bank in Bangladesh, and onward transfer to other banks or mobile financial services.

A user, Saiful Islam, said Hometown's service charge for sending money from Singapore to Bangladesh is only 3 Singapore dollars however much is sent, whereas in other apps the service charge rises with the amount.

Expatriates in Singapore told Go Zayan that to send money cheaply they had to use a bank and go there on a working day; sending larger sums by mobile banking meant extra cost for the family to withdraw at home; the few apps available had high service charges; and hundi carried a security risk and earned no incentive.
About 1 lakh 30 thousand (130,000) Bangladeshi expatriates are in Singapore.

Ridwan Hafiz said 60 percent of tickets on Bangladesh's international flights are bought by expatriates, and that Go Zayan's research found 32 percent of migrant workers had been cheated at least once when buying a ticket and they often pay 20 percent more than the market price.
facts.source_in_article: Ridwan Hafiz, citing Go Zayan's own research

facts.statement: According to Ridwan Hafiz, migrant workers often cannot buy tickets at a fair price because of language difficulties, being unused to online buying, lack of time and falling into the hands of a class of brokers; almost all have smartphones but avoid online payment because it seems complicated.
Hometown currently has a 38 percent market share of Singapore-Bangladesh flights and processes USD 8 million in remittance a month, according to the article.

After Singapore, Hometown is working to expand its service to Malaysia and Saudi Arabia, where it faces different regulations, cash dependence and widely spread communities. Go Zayan itself sells domestic and international air tickets and also operates ticketing in Pakistan.

Bangladeshi expatriates in Singapore gather near Mustafa Mart every Saturday and Sunday and discuss, among other things, how to send money home cheaply, buy tickets and which flights allow more luggage; Go Zayan staff went there on weekends to understand their problems.

headline_en: 20 bodies wash ashore on Libya coast, believed to be Bangladeshis
summary_en: The bodies of 20 would-be migrants were recovered from the Brega shore of the Mediterranean in eastern Libya after a migrant boat sank; the local Red Crescent believes all were Bangladeshi, but the Bangladesh Embassy in Libya could not confirm identities. The decomposing bodies carried no nationality documents and were buried at a place called Ajdadiya, 40 km from Brega.

facts.date: late January 2025 (the two days before Thursday 30 January 2025)
facts.statement: The bodies of 20 would-be migrants were recovered from the Brega shore of the Mediterranean in eastern Libya; local rescue authorities said they washed ashore after a migrant boat sank in the Mediterranean. Most are believed to be Bangladeshi, but identities were not confirmed.
facts.source_in_article: Bangladesh Embassy in Libya (Facebook post of Thursday 30 January 2025)

facts.statement: On Saturday 1 February 2025 the Bangladesh Embassy in Libya said the nationality of the dead was still not confirmed, that the local Red Crescent believes they were all Bangladeshi nationals, and that the embassy had not yet received permission to go to the place where the bodies were recovered.
The bodies found at Brega were decomposing and had no nationality documents with them; as they could not be identified they were buried at a place called Ajdadiya (আজদাদিয়া), 40 km from Brega.

Libya is one of the routes for entering Europe illegally across the Mediterranean; the crossing is made mainly in small boats loaded beyond capacity, and many would-be migrants die on this route every year.

headline_en: Bangladesh is working sincerely to meet Saudi Arabia's demand for skilled workers: Adviser Asif Nazrul
summary_en: A press release on Adviser Asif Nazrul's official visit to Saudi Arabia for the Global Labour Market Conference. At a meeting with Saudi company owners organised by the Bangladesh Embassy in Riyadh he said there is wide scope to send skilled and semi-skilled workers, and he inaugurated the embassy's e-Demand Attestation System. He also heard expatriates' complaints about high air fares and overcharging by recruiting agencies.

facts.statement: Adviser Asif Nazrul inaugurated the Bangladesh Embassy in Riyadh's e-Demand Attestation System, through which Saudi companies can register online and get worker demand letters attested without going to the embassy.

Asif Nazrul said there is wide scope to send skilled and semi-skilled workers including doctors, engineers, nurses and technicians to Saudi Arabia, pointing to Vision 2030 mega projects (NEOM, Red Sea, Qiddiya, Green Riyadh, Amaala, Diriyah and Roshn) and events such as the 2027 AFC Asian Cup, 2029 Asian Winter Games, World Expo 2030 and the 2034 FIFA World Cup.
facts.source_in_article: Adviser Asif Nazrul, via press release

facts.statement: Saudi recruitment companies acknowledged the presence of skilled Bangladeshi professionals but cited challenges: lack of information, marketing, networking, slow visa processing, language barriers and lack of pre-boarding training. Asif Nazrul promised to resolve these and stressed regular labour fairs and seminars.
Bangladeshi expatriates in Saudi Arabia complained to Adviser Asif Nazrul about the high price of air tickets and recruiting agencies collecting extra money; he assured them of solutions.
Asif Nazrul urged expatriates in Saudi Arabia to use social media and the website to increase contact with the embassy, to obey Saudi law and culture and not to get involved in any unlawful activity.
facts.source_in_article: Adviser Asif Nazrul, via press release

facts.statement: On expatriates' voting rights in national elections, Asif Nazrul said the government is examining possible options to reach a realistic decision.

headline_en: Strong effort needed to recover labour markets
summary_en: An editorial noting record remittance of USD 2,670 crore in 2024 but a drop of about 3 lakh in workers sent abroad, to 10 lakh, because three large markets, Malaysia, Oman and the United Arab Emirates, closed. It gives year-by-year deployment figures and calls for diplomatic efforts to reopen the closed markets, legal action against those responsible, and an end to reliance on Saudi Arabia alone.

facts.statement: Remittance to Bangladesh in 2024 was USD 2,670 crore, a record; the previous high was a little over USD 2,200 crore in 2021.

According to BMET, 6 lakh 17 thousand workers went abroad from Bangladesh in 2021, more than 11 lakh in 2022, more than 13 lakh in 2023, and 10 lakh in 2024, a fall of 3 lakh. 90 percent of 2024's workers went to just 5 countries: Saudi Arabia, Malaysia, Qatar, Singapore and the United Arab Emirates.
facts.source_in_article: BMET data, cited in the editorial

facts.statement: More than 3.5 lakh Bangladeshi workers went to Malaysia in 2023, but the market closed from June 2024 and fewer than one lakh could go in all of 2024; not even all those registered to go could go. The editorial says the Malaysian market closed for all countries over allegations of syndicate formation.
More than 1.25 lakh Bangladeshi workers went to Oman in 2023; with the market closed in 2024, only 358 workers went.
About one lakh Bangladeshi workers went to the United Arab Emirates in 2023; in 2024, 47 thousand went.

The editorial says the countries whose markets closed to Bangladeshi workers have not stopped taking workers altogether; bans on Bangladeshi workers were imposed because of irregularities and corruption by manpower-sending firms.

With three large markets closed, Saudi Arabia is described as the only reliance, with sending numbers rising; demand for infrastructure construction workers is expected to grow because Saudi Arabia will host the 2034 football World Cup.

When Malaysia's prime minister made a short visit to Dhaka after the interim government took office, Bangladesh raised the problem of workers unable to go; the editorial says no progress since then is known.

headline_en: 186 workers returned from the Emirates get cheques of BDT 50,000
summary_en: On Saturday 28 December 2024, 186 workers who were jailed in the United Arab Emirates for marching in solidarity with Bangladesh's student movement, then freed and returned, received BDT 50,000 cheques at the Wage Earners' Welfare Board auditorium. Adviser Asif Nazrul promised them top priority in government sending through BOESL and loans on easy terms from Probashi Kallyan Bank. Returnees demanded lifting of the UAE entry ban, release of those still jailed and action against embassy officials.

facts.statement: 186 workers returned from the United Arab Emirates after being jailed for demonstrating in solidarity with the anti-discrimination student movement each received a cheque for BDT 50,000 in cash assistance at the Wage Earners' Welfare Board auditorium on Saturday 28 December 2024.

Adviser Asif Nazrul said the released workers will get the highest priority when the government sends workers abroad through BOESL (Bangladesh Overseas Employment and Services Limited), though getting them jobs abroad again does not depend on the government.
Asif Nazrul said 60 of the returnees had already contacted Probashi Kallyan Bank for loans and that efforts would be made to give loans on easy terms for the workers' rehabilitation.

The workers jailed over the July 2024 protest and returned to Bangladesh face a ban on entering the United Arab Emirates; Asif Nazrul said the ban will not be lifted just by asking and that the Chief Adviser would be requested to speak with the UAE about it.
facts.source_in_article: Adviser Asif Nazrul; returnees' spokesman Khaled Saifullah

facts.statement: Expatriates alleged that some diplomats behaved in a hostile way; Asif Nazrul said action cannot be taken against a government employee on verbal claims alone, and that if a written complaint is given it will be investigated through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. He invited a seven-member delegation of returnees to the ministry at 3 pm on 29 December 2024 to discuss their complaints.

Expatriates in the UAE marched on 19 July 2024; UAE law does not allow such protest without permission. Initially 57 people were detained in one case and then 56 in another; they were pardoned in stages, and 186 people detained in several cases had been freed under general pardon and returned home by late December 2024.

facts.statement: Returnees say expatriates are still being detained in different parts of the UAE over the July 2024 protest and that people remain in jail; Bangladesh Embassy sources in the UAE say they currently have no complaint of anyone being detained.

headline_en: Overseas employment rising again on the back of Saudi Arabia
summary_en: After falling in early 2024 and dropping further when Malaysia closed in June, monthly overseas deployment from Bangladesh rose again in October and November 2024, driven by Saudi Arabia, which took 60 percent of the year's workers and over 80 percent in the last two months. The article explains the Saudi kafil (sponsor) rule and reports experts' proposals such as ending embassy attestation of demand letters and registering brokers.

facts.statement: According to BMET, more than 11 lakh workers went abroad from Bangladesh in 2022, 13 lakh in 2023, and 9 lakh in the first 11 months of 2024, which may reach 10 lakh by year end, 3 lakh fewer than 2023. More than 2 lakh went in October and November 2024 together.
60 percent of workers who went abroad from Bangladesh in 2024 went to Saudi Arabia, and more than 80 percent of overseas employment in October-November 2024 was in Saudi Arabia.
People concerned say demand for workers from Saudi Arabia is coming regularly because it will host the 2034 football World Cup and has begun preparing to build football infrastructure.
facts.source_in_article: unnamed people concerned; BAIRA secretary general Ali Haider Chowdhury

facts.statement: To go to Saudi Arabia a worker must go through an employer or kafil; no worker can go without a specific employer, and once there must work under that employer, otherwise the worker is treated as illegal. To change jobs for any reason, the worker must get the employer's permission and the Saudi authorities' approval.

Malaysia's labour market has been closed to Bangladeshi workers since June 2024; Expatriates' Welfare Secretary Md. Ruhul Amin said in December 2024 that a meeting of the two countries would be held soon to reopen it.
Expatriates' Welfare Secretary Md. Ruhul Amin said Brunei has been opened, workers are going to Russia, and because Europe has high demand for skilled workers the emphasis is on raising skills.

Experts say the government should stop attestation of worker demand letters by embassies in destination countries and make recruiting agencies accountable instead, ensure services from embassy labour wings, create a separate cadre under the Expatriates' Welfare Ministry because administration-cadre officers serve in labour wings only temporarily, and bring brokers under registration to legalise them.

RMMRU founding chair Tasneem Siddiqui said dependence on particular labour markets is the biggest weakness, that there is now no scope to form a syndicate as before, and that even if fewer workers go, a job must be ensured for every one of them by holding recruiting agencies accountable.

BAIRA secretary general Ali Haider Chowdhury said the labour market is shrinking and workers are now going mainly to Saudi Arabia; to hold on to this, a meeting of the two countries' technical committee should be called to discuss existing problems.

headline_en: Formulating and implementing a national migration policy
summary_en: An opinion piece by an expatriate writer (who refers to Tokyo) arguing that Bangladesh should merge its expatriates' welfare and overseas employment policy and its draft national diaspora policy into one national migration policy made in consultation with expatriate communities. It mentions the separate airport counter/expatriate lounge implemented by the interim government, the BMET smart card introduced in 2010 for BDT 250 and suspended in February 2024 over forgery, and the definitions of NRB and PoB in the draft diaspora policy.

facts.statement: The 2016 Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment Policy said separate immigration counters should be set up at airports for migrant workers so that departure and return data can be kept; the writer says the interim government implemented this after eight years, and a special expatriates' lounge was opened at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport, arranged by Adviser Asif Nazrul, with the Chief Adviser inviting opinions at its inauguration.

In 2010 the Bureau of Manpower, Employment and Training (BMET) began issuing the immigration clearance card or smart card for a fee of BDT 250; according to the writer, because of repeated forgery by manpower brokers the activity was temporarily suspended in February 2024.
The Overseas Employment and Migrants Act made in 2013 defines those who go to another country to take up an occupation as 'migrants' (অভিবাসী).

The Expatriates' Welfare Ministry began framing a National Diaspora Policy in 2023, which as of November 2024 remained a revised draft. The draft divides expatriates into Non-Resident Bangladeshis (NRB), who have lived abroad long-term but have not obtained citizenship (passport) or civic rights, and People of Bangladeshi Origin (PoB), who or whose later generations have obtained another country's citizenship.
facts.source_in_article: the columnist, describing the draft policy

facts.statement: The writer states that the most remittance to Bangladesh is now coming from the United States, where diaspora members far outnumber migrant workers.

IOM's Dhaka office began operating in 1998; IOM became a UN-related organisation in 2016, and in 2018 the 23 objectives of the Global Compact for Migration were declared, covering prevention of human trafficking, legal remittance, empowerment of migrants, skills development and dignified return. The writer says IOM's Dhaka office has lately been speaking loudly about migration management and human trafficking from Bangladesh.

The writer proposes moving overseas employment to the Ministry of Labour and Employment, including migrant workers' welfare in the work of the interim government's Labour Reform Commission, and issuing a separate free card to identify expatriates if the airport lounge is meant for all expatriates. These are the writer's proposals.

The writer alleges that for several years under the previous government the Bangladesh Embassy in Tokyo did not invite expatriates linked to opposition politics to state events, and that after the interim government came those close to the previous government are less welcome; he says embassies must not discriminate among expatriates. He also says Adviser Asif Nazrul was recently harassed by some expatriates at Geneva airport.

headline_en: 157 Bangladeshis return home from Libya
summary_en: 157 irregular Bangladeshi nationals who wished to return voluntarily from Misrata and nearby areas of Libya arrived in Dhaka on a Buraq Air charter flight at 4:25 am on Tuesday 22 October 2024, with help from the foreign ministry, the Bangladesh Embassy in Tripoli and IOM. Most had gone to Libya with traffickers' help intending to reach Europe by sea, and many were kidnapped and tortured there. IOM gave each returnee BDT 6,000 and some food.

facts.statement: 157 irregular Bangladeshi nationals returned from Libya on a Buraq Air chartered flight that landed at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport, Dhaka at 4:25 am on Tuesday 22 October 2024; they were received by officials of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and IOM.

The 157 were irregular Bangladeshis from Misrata and neighbouring areas of Libya who wished to return voluntarily; they were brought back with the cooperation of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Bangladesh Embassy in Tripoli and IOM.

Most of the returnees had gone to Libya at the instigation and with the help of human traffickers, intending to go illegally to Europe by sea; many of them were kidnapped and tortured in Libya at various times.
IOM gave each person returning from Libya BDT 6,000 and some food as a gift, and arranged medical treatment and, where needed, temporary accommodation.
Foreign ministry officials urged the returnees to be aware themselves and make everyone aware so that no one else goes to Libya by this dangerous route.
The Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Bangladesh Embassy in Tripoli and IOM are working together to arrange the safe return of Bangladeshi nationals held in various detention centres in Libya.

headline_en: Man trafficked to Libya rescued with PBI's help
summary_en: Syed Abdus Salam (42), a farmer from Bagherpara, Jashore, was promised Romania and then Italy by his neighbour Nawab Ali for BDT 4 lakh, flown via Dubai and Egypt to Libya in March 2023, confined and tortured, and his family was made to pay BDT 15 lakh in ransom. After his wife filed a trafficking case on 2 May 2024, the PBI investigator contacted Nawab Ali, who arranged his return; he came home on 13 September 2024 and gave a court statement on 22 September.

facts.statement: Nawab Ali, a neighbour of farmer Syed Abdus Salam in Jashore, first said he could send him to Romania, then said he would send him to Italy instead, and made a deal with him for BDT 4 lakh.
Syed Abdus Salam of Bagherpara, Jashore paid neighbour Nawab Ali the agreed BDT 4 lakh to be sent to Italy.

After getting the money, Nawab Ali took Salam on 22 March 2023 through Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport to Dubai, where they stayed two days, then to Egypt, and after a five-hour stop in Egypt to Libya, where Nawab Ali kept him confined inside a house.

After 20-22 days in Libya, Nawab Ali sent Salam to some unknown people supposedly to be sent to Italy; they told him to contact two men named Nadim and Hasan, who confined him at an unknown place and tortured him physically and mentally to extract ransom.
The captors in Libya collected BDT 15 lakh from Salam's family at various times as ransom.
Salam's wife filed a case in court under the human trafficking law on 2 May 2024 to get him rescued; the court ordered PBI Jashore to investigate.

The investigating officer, PBI (Jashore) Inspector Mir Rezaul Hossain, contacted the accused Nawab Ali, who was abroad; Nawab Ali put the officer in touch with Salam by video call and then arranged to send Salam back from Libya. Salam returned to Bangladesh on 13 September 2024.

On Sunday 22 September 2024 Syed Abdus Salam gave a statement in court under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure; PBI (Jashore) Superintendent of Police Reshma Sharmin said efforts are under way to arrest those involved.

headline_en: Tickets worth BDT 20-25 thousand now cost over a lakh
summary_en: With the 31 May 2024 deadline for new Bangladeshi workers to enter Malaysia approaching, Dhaka-Kuala Lumpur air fares rose from the usual BDT 20-25 thousand to over BDT 1 lakh and all seats sold out. A travel agency complained to the Prime Minister's Office that Biman officials were taking bribes of BDT 20-25 thousand per ticket to release special-flight seats; Biman denied it and said its special-flight fares started at BDT 68,000. BAIRA says a worker is already spending BDT 4.5-5 lakh to go to Malaysia because of the syndicate.

facts.statement: The time for new Bangladeshi workers to go to Malaysia ends on 31 May 2024: Malaysia closed its labour market again but gave already-approved workers until 31 May to enter the country.

The highest price of a Dhaka-Kuala Lumpur air ticket is normally BDT 20 to 25 thousand; in normal times the cheapest ticket from Dhaka to Malaysia is BDT 24 to 25 thousand, while from Kolkata it is BDT 14 to 15 thousand, though the flight time is 3 hours 55 minutes from Dhaka and four hours from Kolkata.

From the start of May 2024 the Dhaka-Kuala Lumpur fare more than tripled; by mid-month it was BDT 80 thousand to 1 lakh; by 27 May no airline had empty seats and the fare on Biman's special flights also exceeded BDT 1 lakh.

Biman Bangladesh Airlines operated four special flights to Malaysia for the workers; Biman sources said special-flight tickets started from BDT 68 thousand, with the higher price set because the return flights from Malaysia would come back empty, and that tickets were open to all and could be bought online. Biman wrote to Malaysia on Sunday 26 May 2024 for permission for four more special flights and had no reply by 4 pm on 27 May.

Ether Fariel Hamid, managing director of Fariel Tours and Travels, complained to the Prime Minister's Office that agencies could not book Biman's special Malaysia flights directly because the tickets were not showing in the Global Distribution System (GDS), and Biman officials were using this for corruption. She told Prothom Alo tickets were opened in GDS on payment of a bribe of BDT 20 to 25 thousand per ticket, pushing the price to BDT 1 lakh 5 thousand to 1 lakh 10 thousand.
facts.source_in_article: Ether Fariel Hamid, Fariel Tours and Travels

facts.statement: Biman's acting director of marketing and sales Mohammad Salahuddin said special-flight tickets were opened by announcement four days earlier, 99 percent were sold through GDS, that naming who took bribes would help action, and that any agency charging more than BDT 1 lakh for a ticket should have its licence cancelled.
Prothom Alo tried several times on 26 and 27 May 2024 to get a ticket on Biman's website and found all tickets from 27 to 31 May showing 'sold out'.

Malaysia's labour market reopened in July 2022 after being closed for about four years; since then more than 4.5 lakh Bangladeshi workers have gone there. Several international organisations alleged irregularities in sending, workers not getting jobs after arrival and labour exploitation, and Malaysia closed the market again.

BAIRA says workers already bear extra cost to go to Malaysia because of the syndicate of selected agencies: a worker is spending BDT 4.5 to 5 lakh, and the abnormal ticket price adds to that; it was still uncertain whether all workers could be sent in time.

ATAB (Association of Travel Agents of Bangladesh) said airlines charge extra citing fuel costs and raise fares further at festival times, private and foreign airlines follow when state carrier Biman raises fares, and the expatriates' welfare ministry should have told airlines in advance how many workers would go to Malaysia in May. ATAB president Abdus Salam Aref said a BDT 30 thousand ticket cannot be BDT 1 lakh and called it oppression of passengers; ATAB wrote to airlines requesting extra Malaysia flights.

headline_en: Bodies of eight Bangladeshis who died in the Mediterranean handed over to families
summary_en: The bodies of eight Bangladeshis from Madaripur and Gopalganj who died in the Mediterranean on 14 February 2024 while going from Libya to Italy were flown to Dhaka on 2 May 2024 and handed to relatives from the Dhaka Medical College morgue on 3 May. Relatives said brokers put 52 people on a small boat meant for 30 and forced the eight below deck, where they died from lack of oxygen and beatings.

facts.statement: Eight Bangladeshis died in the Mediterranean on 14 February 2024 while going from Libya to Italy.

The eight bodies were flown from Libya to Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport at midday on Thursday 2 May 2024, and on Friday afternoon 3 May 2024 police handed them to family members from the Dhaka Medical College morgue in the presence of an executive magistrate.

The bodies had already been autopsied in Tunisia; the autopsy reports were checked in the presence of Dhaka district executive magistrate Sayem Imran and a forensic doctor before the bodies were handed to relatives, said the investigating officer, Sub-Inspector Jahangir Alam of Airport police station, Dhaka.
facts.source_in_article: SI Jahangir Alam, Airport police station, Dhaka

facts.statement: Relatives of the dead said brokers put 52 people on a small boat that could carry 30 for the Libya-Italy crossing; the eight who died had been forced to stay under the boat's deck, tried to come out because of lack of oxygen, and were beaten by the brokers and sent back down; they died of torture and lack of oxygen, as the relatives had heard.
facts.source_in_article: relatives of the dead, speaking at the airport on 2 May 2024

facts.statement: The eight dead were: from Rajoir thana, Madaripur, Sajal Bairagi (22) of Sendia village and Nayan Biswas (18) of Kadambari village, son of the late Paritosh Biswas; Mamun Sheikh (24) of Sarmangal village, Kazi Sajib (18) of Kodalia village, and Kaiser Khalifa (35) of Keshardia village, son of Tota Khalifa; and from Muksudpur thana, Gopalganj, Rifat Sheikh (24), son of Dadan Sheikh, Rasel Sheikh (25) of Padmapatti village, son of Abul Kashem Sheikh, and Imrul Kayes Apon (23) of Padmapatti village, son of Pannu Sheikh.

headline_en: How do we increase remittance through legal channels
summary_en: A column by banker Mamun Rashid on raising remittance through legal channels. It reports the parliamentary standing committee on the expatriates' welfare ministry listing ten obstacles to sending money legally, gives district-wise overseas employment figures, and cites a former finance minister saying only 51 percent of potential remittance arrives legally, the rest through hundi.

facts.statement: Former finance minister A H M Mustafa Kamal said only 51 percent of Bangladesh's potential or estimated remittance comes through legal channels and the rest through hundi; on that basis, with USD 22-23 billion currently received, estimated remittance is USD 40-42 billion.
facts.source_in_article: A H M Mustafa Kamal, quoted by the columnist

facts.statement: A meeting of the parliamentary standing committee on the expatriates' welfare ministry listed 10 obstacles to sending remittance legally: a sizeable exchange-rate gap between legal and illegal channels; expatriate workers lacking valid papers; no or too few branches of Bangladeshi commercial banks abroad; no or too few Bangladeshi money exchange houses or points; high fees or service charges and set ceilings on sending; the dominance of hundi traders; expatriates or their close relatives often having no bank account in Bangladesh; obstacles when the amount sent is not consistent with income; no way to send income from unauthorised business or work legally; and lack of awareness and encouragement.
facts.source_in_article: parliamentary standing committee meeting, as reported by the columnist

facts.statement: According to the committee document, in fiscal year 2023-24 the most people went abroad for employment from Cumilla district, 80,572; then Brahmanbaria 49,391, Chattogram 43,008, Tangail 38,712, Chandpur 34,956, Kishoreganj 32,907, Noakhali 30,841, Mymensingh 30,080, Narsingdi 30,029 and Dhaka 26,883.
facts.source_in_article: parliamentary standing committee meeting, as reported by the columnist

facts.statement: The same parliamentary committee meeting recommended timely training for people going abroad, help in getting loans, the best possible service to resolve problems arising from workers' deaths abroad, exploring new labour markets, and taking initiatives to send workers at zero migration cost where reasonable or necessary, in line with migration policy; it also recommended awareness measures for legal remittance and steps against hundi traders.
facts.source_in_article: parliamentary standing committee, as reported by the columnist

facts.statement: The columnist explains how hundi works: the foreign currency (Saudi riyal, UAE dirham or other) does not come to Bangladesh but an equal amount, or even 5 to 10 percent more, arrives in taka, and expatriates' relatives at home are even given advance loans; the foreign currency goes to another country for under-invoicing, evading import tax or moving assets abroad.

The columnist recalls learning at a Bangladesh Enterprise Institute (BEI) discussion in 2004-2005 that Bangladesh's potential remittance was then about USD 20 billion, of which about USD 11-12 billion was coming through banking channels.

The columnist says Bangladesh missions abroad must be more active, World Bank help could be taken, and action may be needed against some commercial banks or their officials involved in cleverly encouraging hundi.
